dependent_variable.name: ILLIQ
dependent_variable.definition: Combined illiquidity measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of available ZERORET and LN(BIDASK); if BIDASK is unavailable, use the percentile rank of ZERORET. ZERORET is the percent of fiscal-year trading days with no price change. BIDASK is the fiscal-year median relative bid–ask spread, (ASK−BID)/((ASK+BID)/2), and LN(BIDASK) is the transformed component. The reference population and scaling convention for “scaled percentile rank” are not reported.
dependent_variable.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ZERORET), scaled_percentile_rank(ln(BIDASK))) when BIDASK available; scaled_percentile_rank(ZERORET) otherwise

evidence.quote: The dependent variable in all models is ILLIQ, which is a combined measure of illiquidity equal to the average scaled percentile rank of the available liquidity measures, ZERORET and LN(BIDASK). If BIDASK is unavailable, ILLIQ captures the percentile rank of ZERORET.
ZERORET is equal to the percent of days in the fiscal year for which the stock price does not change
BIDASK is equal to the median bid ask spread over the fiscal year, where the bid ask spread is equal to (ASK−BID)/((ASK+BID)/2)).

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

models.equation_text: ILLIQ_t = α_t + β1 LNMVE_t + β2 BM_t + β3 LOSS_t + β4 STDRET_t + β5 ADR_EX_t + β6 ADR_NEX_t + β7 %CLHLD_H_t + β8 %CLHLD_L_t + β9 FUND_SMTHC_t + β10 TRANS_t + FIXED EFFECTS + ε_t

fixed_effects.details: Country, industry, and year fixed effects; industry fixed effects use the firm’s two-digit ICB code.

evidence.quote: We include country (C), industry (I), and year (Y) fixed effects in all models, but do not report the coefficients. Industry fixed effects are based on the firm’s two-digit ICB code.

standard_errors.details: Two-sided p-values use robust standard errors clustered at firm level (one clustering dimension); this fit has 4,714 firm clusters. Table 5 cross-partition tests use a different country-industry cluster, as recorded in estimation_procedure.

evidence.quote: The table reports OLS coefficient estimates and p-values (two-sided) based on robust standard errors clustered at the firm-level.

estimation_procedure.description: Table 5 Panel A reports a separate OLS fit for the LOW ASDI partition; its grouping dimension is ASDI relative to the sample median. The table’s cross-partition HIGH–LOW coefficient test is based on a fully interacted specification that lets all variables and fixed effects vary by partition and clusters standard errors at the country-industry level; the table reports 589 country-industry clusters for this comparison. This comparison fit is described in the source but has no separately printed full equation.
grouping_variables: ASDI relative to the country-level sample median

evidence.quote: In panel A, regressions are run separately for high and low ASDI, DISCLOSE, and MEDIA subgroups

Assessments of significance across partitions are made based on the standard errors (clustered at the country-industry level) of the coefficient on the interaction of TRANS and the partitioning variable in a fully interacted specification, i.e., we allow each variable, including the fixed effects, to vary by the partitioning variable.

preprocessing.description: All continuous nonlogarithmic variables are truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles.

evidence.quote: All continuous nonlogarithmic variables are truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.
one of our primary goals is to document the extent to which the importance of firm-level transparency varies with a firm’s characteristics and its environment.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
Our primary interest is in comparing the strength of the relation between TRANS and ILLIQ across the high and low ASDI, DISCLOSE, and MEDIA subsamples.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.
one of our primary goals is to document the extent to which the importance of firm-level transparency varies with a firm’s characteristics and its environment.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
Our primary interest is in comparing the strength of the relation between TRANS and ILLIQ across the high and low ASDI, DISCLOSE, and MEDIA subsamples.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

evidence.quote: We include country (C), industry (I), and year (Y) fixed effects in all models, but do not report the coefficients. Industry fixed effects are based on the firm’s two-digit ICB code.

standard_errors.details: Two-sided p-values use robust standard errors clustered at firm level (one clustering dimension); this fit has 2,530 firm clusters. Adjacent-group comparison tests cluster at country-industry level, as described in estimation_procedure.

evidence.quote: The table reports OLS coefficient estimates and p-values (two-sided) based on robust standard errors clustered at the firm-level.

estimation_procedure.description: Table 5 Panel B runs separate OLS regressions for GOV SCORE groups 0, 1, 2, and 3. The adjacent-group RIGHT–LEFT coefficient tests use fully interacted specifications that let every variable and fixed effect vary across the comparison, with country-industry clustered standard errors; the table reports 436, 348, and 201 country-industry clusters for the adjacent comparisons. The source does not print a separate full equation for those comparison fits.

evidence.quote: In panel B, regressions are run separately for GOV SCORE subgroups.

GOV SCORE is an aggregate variable composed of the three country-level institutional variables in panel A where a country receives a value of one for each of the individual institutional variables for which it is above the sample median with possible scores taking integer values between 0 and 3.

Assessments of significance across partitions are made based on the standard errors (clustered at the country-industry level) of the coefficient on the interaction of TRANS and the partitioning variable in a fully interacted specification, i.e., we allow each variable, including the fixed effects, to vary by the partitioning variable.

preprocessing.description: All continuous nonlogarithmic variables are truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.
one of our primary goals is to document the extent to which the importance of firm-level transparency varies with a firm’s characteristics and its environment.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
There are two primary takeaways from this analysis.
the magnitude of the TRANS coefficient increases monotonically, moving across partitions from strongest to weakest overall governance environments.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

fixed_effects.details: Country, industry, and year fixed effects; industry fixed effects use the firm’s two-digit ICB code.

evidence.quote: We include country (C), industry (I), and year (Y) fixed effects in all models, but do not report the coefficients. Industry fixed effects are based on the firm’s two-digit ICB code.

standard_errors.details: Two-sided p-values use robust standard errors clustered at firm level (one clustering dimension); this fit has 3,255 firm clusters. Adjacent-group comparison tests cluster at country-industry level, as described in estimation_procedure.

evidence.quote: The table reports OLS coefficient estimates and p-values (two-sided) based on robust standard errors clustered at the firm-level.

estimation_procedure.description: Table 5 Panel B runs separate OLS regressions for GOV SCORE groups 0, 1, 2, and 3. The adjacent-group RIGHT–LEFT coefficient tests use fully interacted specifications that let every variable and fixed effect vary across the comparison, with country-industry clustered standard errors; the table reports 436, 348, and 201 country-industry clusters for the adjacent comparisons. The source does not print a separate full equation for those comparison fits.

evidence.quote: In panel B, regressions are run separately for GOV SCORE subgroups.

GOV SCORE is an aggregate variable composed of the three country-level institutional variables in panel A where a country receives a value of one for each of the individual institutional variables for which it is above the sample median with possible scores taking integer values between 0 and 3.

Assessments of significance across partitions are made based on the standard errors (clustered at the country-industry level) of the coefficient on the interaction of TRANS and the partitioning variable in a fully interacted specification, i.e., we allow each variable, including the fixed effects, to vary by the partitioning variable.

preprocessing.description: All continuous nonlogarithmic variables are truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles.

evidence.quote: All continuous nonlogarithmic variables are truncated at the 1st and 99th percentiles.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.
one of our primary goals is to document the extent to which the importance of firm-level transparency varies with a firm’s characteristics and its environment.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
There are two primary takeaways from this analysis.
the magnitude of the TRANS coefficient increases monotonically, moving across partitions from strongest to weakest overall governance environments.

method.quote: The table reports OLS coefficient estimates and p-values (two-sided) based on robust standard errors clustered at the firm-level.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

estimation_procedure.description: Table 5 Panel B runs separate OLS regressions for GOV SCORE groups 0, 1, 2, and 3. The adjacent-group RIGHT–LEFT coefficient tests use fully interacted specifications that let every variable and fixed effect vary across the comparison, with country-industry clustered standard errors; the table reports 436, 348, and 201 country-industry clusters for the adjacent comparisons. The source does not print a separate full equation for those comparison fits.

evidence.quote: In panel B, regressions are run separately for GOV SCORE subgroups.

GOV SCORE is an aggregate variable composed of the three country-level institutional variables in panel A where a country receives a value of one for each of the individual institutional variables for which it is above the sample median with possible scores taking integer values between 0 and 3.

Assessments of significance across partitions are made based on the standard errors (clustered at the country-industry level) of the coefficient on the interaction of TRANS and the partitioning variable in a fully interacted specification, i.e., we allow each variable, including the fixed effects, to vary by the partitioning variable.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.
one of our primary goals is to document the extent to which the importance of firm-level transparency varies with a firm’s characteristics and its environment.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
There are two primary takeaways from this analysis.
the magnitude of the TRANS coefficient increases monotonically, moving across partitions from strongest to weakest overall governance environments.

ZERORET is equal to the percent of days in the fiscal year for which the stock price does not change

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

evidence.quote: TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.
For parsimony in our later analyses, we combine the transparency variables to create an aggregate measure, TRANS, by ranking each variable, summing the percentile ranks, and taking the average.

estimation_procedure.description: Table 5 Panel B runs separate OLS regressions for GOV SCORE groups 0, 1, 2, and 3. evidence.quote: In panel B, regressions are run separately for GOV SCORE subgroups.

GOV SCORE is an aggregate variable composed of the three country-level institutional variables in panel A where a country receives a value of one for each of the individual institutional variables for which it is above the sample median with possible scores taking integer values between 0 and 3.

Assessments of significance across partitions are made based on the standard errors (clustered at the country-industry level) of the coefficient on the interaction of TRANS and the partitioning variable in a fully interacted specification, i.e., we allow each variable, including the fixed effects, to vary by the partitioning variable.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.
one of our primary goals is to document the extent to which the importance of firm-level transparency varies with a firm’s characteristics and its environment.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
There are two primary takeaways from this analysis.
the magnitude of the TRANS coefficient increases monotonically, moving across partitions from strongest to weakest overall governance environments.

independent_variables.name: TRANS
independent_variables.definition: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported. In Table 6, this annual measure is taken from the preceding year and treated as representative for the following 12 months.
independent_variables.formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks

Model 3 includes year and firm fixed effects, showing that, even within a firm, transparency matters more in time periods with higher uncertainty, which suggests that our results do not simply reflect other cross-firm differences.

scope.quote: Our primary interest is in variation in the strength of the relation between firm-level transparency and liquidity across economic environments.

We consider three aspects of the firm’s environment that are likely to increase investor demand for information: poor country-level institutions, time periods with high aggregate levels of investor uncertainty, and firm-level governance problems.
As a result, the question we ask is whether, following a month of high country-level uncertainty, firm-level illiquidity is more sensitive to transparency.

ILLIQ t = αt + β 1 LNMVE t + β 2 BM t + β 3 LOSS t + β 4 STDRET t + β 5 ADR EX t + β 6 ADR NEX t


+ β 7% CLHLD ~~H~~ t + β 8% CLHLD ~~L~~ t + β 9 FUND ~~S~~ MTHC t


+ β 10% CLHLD H <sup>∗</sup> TRANS t + β 11% CLHLD ~~L~~ <sup>∗</sup> TRANS t + FIXED EFFECTS + εt

Accordingly, we define serious adopters ( INTGAAP S = 1), our final transparency indicator, to be adopting firms that have an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable) and either a) are mandated by country regulations to adopt international accounting standards, or b) voluntarily adopted international standards
ANALYST is equal to the average number of analysts making a forecast for year t ’s earnings over the SMTH estimation period

ACCURACY is the absolute value of the forecast error multiplied by −1, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S

BIAS is the signed value of the forecast error, scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year, where the forecast error is the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast less the actual earnings as reported by I/B/E/S
SUE is the absolute value of unexpected earnings, scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year, where unexpected earnings is actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast
BIG5 is equal to one if the firm is audited by a “BIG5” auditing firm, and zero otherwise
R ACCURACY is equal to the residual value from a regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS.

INTGAAP S is an indicator variable equal to one if the firm reports under IFRS or U.S. GAAP during the year and has an above-median aggregate transparency score (calculated excluding the INTGAAP variable).
DIS SMTHC is the average of the scaled percentile rank of DIS SMTH1 and DIS SMTH2, where DIS SMTH1 & 2 are the residual values from the fundamental earnings smoothness model described in appendix A.

TRANS is defined as the average of the scaled percentile rank of the variables: ANALYST, R ACCURACY , INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC). If R ACCURACY is unavailable, TRANS captures the average percentile rank of the remaining four measures.

dependent_variable.name: SMTH1
dependent_variable.definition: Negative of the ratio of the rolling standard deviation of income before extraordinary items scaled by average total assets to the rolling standard deviation of cash flow from operations scaled by average total assets; rolling calculation requires at least three and at most five years. Cash flow from operations equals income before extraordinary items minus accruals; accruals equal change in current assets minus change in current liabilities minus change in cash plus change in current debt in current liabilities minus depreciation and amortization. Larger values (closer to zero) indicate smoother earnings.
dependent_variable.formula: − SD(NI before extraordinary items / average total assets) / SD(CFO / average total assets)

evidence.quote: SMTH1 is measured as the standard deviation of net income before extraordinary items divided by the standard deviation of cash flow from operations, where net income before extraordinary items and cash flow from operations are scaled by average total assets and the standard deviations are calculated using rolling time intervals requiring a minimum of three and a maximum of five years of data.

Cash flow from operations is equal to net income before extraordinary items minus accruals, where accruals are defined as the change in current assets minus the change in current liabilities minus the change in cash plus the change in current debt in current liabilities minus depreciation and amortization expense.
Both smoothing measures ( SMTH1, SMTH2 ) are multiplied by negative one so that larger values represent firms with smoother earnings.

dependent_variable.name: SMTH2
dependent_variable.definition: Negative of the level correlation between cash flow from operations and total accruals. Table 2 says both inputs are scaled by average total assets, whereas Appendix A says total assets; the denominator wording conflicts. It is calculated over rolling windows requiring at least three and at most five years, and larger values (closer to one) indicate smoother earnings.

evidence.quote: The second earnings smoothness measure ( SMTH2 ) is the correlation between the cash flow from operations scaled by total assets and total accruals scaled by total assets.

SMTH2 is defined as the correlation between the cash flow from operations and total accruals, where both measures are scaled by average total assets and correlations are calculated using a minimum of three and maximum of five years of data; SMTH2 is multiplied by negative one so that larger values, i.e., values closer to one, represent smoother earnings.
Both smoothing measures ( SMTH1, SMTH2 ) are multiplied by negative one so that larger values represent firms with smoother earnings.

review_notes: Source-first scope: the authors state that their primary interest is variation in the transparency–liquidity relation across economic environments. Retain the full-control “when transparency matters most” family: Table 5 Panel A’s three country-institution splits (ASDI, DISCLOSE, MEDIA), Panel B’s four GOV SCORE groups, Table 6’s within-firm Model 3, and Table 7’s full-sample column 1. The partition regressions are the author’s chosen design for Table 5; Table 6 Model 3 is the within-firm time-uncertainty design; Table 7 column 1 is the full-sample piecewise-ownership interaction design.

Source inconsistency in Table 5: Table 2 and the Panel A note say lower MEDIA ranks correspond to better media penetration and define HIGH MEDIA as a rank above the median. The surrounding narrative describes the larger transparency coefficient as occurring in weak media-penetration environments, while the printed low-rank coefficient is more negative than the high-rank coefficient. GOV SCORE also counts above-median values for all three indices without stating a direction reversal for MEDIA, yet the discussion interprets the combined score as a governance-strength ranking. Preserve the formula and group labels; do not silently recode MEDIA.

Excluded the prior Table 3–4 direct-association columns because the source identifies contextual variation as its primary interest; excluded Tables 8–9 valuation/cost-of-capital analyses, Appendix B component decompositions, the Table 7 ASDI split columns 2–3, and the Table 6 alternative fixed-effects columns 1–2. These are direct-baseline, downstream, decomposition, or additional partition/design analyses rather than the selected principal family.

Counted and checked every retained RHS term against the source equations and table rows: 10 terms for each Table 5 subgroup fit; 12 terms for Table 6 Model 3; and 11 terms for Table 7 column 1. Table 7 column 1 has no standalone TRANS regressor; TRANS occurs only in the two piecewise ownership interactions.

Table 5 subgroup coefficients are separately estimated. The cross-partition p-values use a fully interacted comparison with all variables and fixed effects varying by the partition and country-industry clustered standard errors. The source does not print that comparison equation separately; it is described in each model’s estimation procedure and was not fabricated as an additional regression record.

Retained the actually fitted SMTH1/SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness regressions and the ACCURACY-on-SUE-and-BIAS residualization fit because their predictions/residuals feed FUND SMTHC and TRANS. No other fitted construction is required for these retained variables.
